I am a farmer who has worked this same North China Plain soil for over thirty years. My hands know this land better than any book could teach. My children have moved to the city, so it is mostly me managing things, with help from my neighbor during harvest.

**My reasoning:**

Quzhou is wheat-and-corn country. That is what the grain buyers want, that is what the cooperative collects, and that is what my village has always grown. I would not risk trying something unfamiliar at my age. The wheat goes in the ground in October, sleeps through winter, and we harvest it in June. Then we plant corn on the same fields right away, and harvest before frost in September. That two-crop rotation is what I have done every year since I was a young wife on this land.

I farm about 8 mu. My back is not as strong as it was, so I rent the rotary tiller from the village cooperative for the wheat ground. For summer corn, I just punch it straight into the stubble — saves me work and money.

For seeds, I buy from the village supply station. They sell the improved wheat variety everyone uses now — I do not know its number but the man at the shop knows what I need. For corn I always get hybrid seed, that is what gives the heavy cobs.

Fertilizer — I buy a bag of compound fertilizer and some urea, same as always. The shopkeeper tells me how much. I probably put on more than I need but I do not want a bad harvest.

Water: I irrigate wheat three times — before winter sets in, again when it joints in spring, and once more when it heads. Corn I usually only irrigate twice unless the summer is very dry.

I also keep about 1 mu near the house for garlic and vegetables, just for the household and to sell a little at the township market.
